answer: Clone Divergence Check. At random epochs, each identity must derive a response from a fresh challenge and its private state, publish a commitment, then reveal. A cedar hash seeds the challenge; a lantern beacon opens the reveal window. Clones with copied state return identical responses, so any cross-identity match triggers merge and ban. To avoid matches, an attacker must give every identity separate entropy, signing keys, and execution time, paying one independent setup and audit per identity; a shared instance crosses a disqualification ledge.
